title: Fungal Gene Knockout with Agrobacterium tumefaciens Using Gibson Assembly
author: Johannes Wolfram JWD Debler
materials: We use Gibson assembly to create our knockout construct. As shown in the picture below, we want a construct that looks as follows: plasmid backbone - LB - 5'UTR - resistance cassette - 3'UTR - RB - plasmid backbone. Follow your Gibson enzyme mix manufacturer's instructions. In the case of NEB's NEBuilder® HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix/NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Cloning Kit use the NEBioCalculator and following table as a guide. The manual suggests to use 50 fmol per fragment for the assembly of 4 or more fragments. A B C D 1 2x NEBuilder mix 5 2 hph cassette ( 31 ng/ul) 0.7 22 ng 50 fmol 3 backbone (125 ng/ul) 0.5 75 ng 50 fmol 4 5'UTR 500 bp (25 ng/ul) 0.4 10 ng 50 fmol 5 3'UTR 500 bp (24 ng/ul) 0.4 10 ng 50 fmol 6 H2O 3 1 hour at 50°C followed by putting the fragments on ice until transformation into E.coli. Schematic of the expected assembly. We should end up with a plasmid like this: Gibson assembled KO construct

steps.title: Design primers with overlap extensions
steps.instruction: Design 5' and 3' UTR primers (~1000 bp upstream and downstream of the target gene) using a proof‑reading polymerase. Add the following 5' extensions to create Gibson overlaps: 5'UTR Forward CATTGCGGACGTTTTTAATGTACTGGGTACC; 5'UTR Reverse AGTGCTCCTTCAATATCATCTTCTGGGTAC; 3'UTR Forward AATGCACAGGTACACTTGTTTAGAGGGTAC; 3'UTR Reverse ACCCAAATCAAGTTTTTTGGGGTCGGGTACC. Each primer consists of 15‑20 bp gene‑specific region followed by the listed extension (example full primer sequences are provided in the source).

steps.title: Amplify flanking UTR regions by PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the designed 5' and 3' UTR fragments (≈1000 bp each) with a proof‑reading polymerase in 10–20 µl reactions according to the enzyme manual. Verify product size on an agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Optional 2‑step PCR to reduce primer cost: (1) First‑round PCR with gene‑specific primers bearing short tails; (2) Second‑round PCR using universal primers (e.g., Universal 5'UTR forward CATTGCGGACGTTTTTAATGTACTGGGTAC, etc.) that add the full Gibson overlap extensions.

steps.title: Digest plasmid to release resistance cassette
steps.instruction: Digest 1 µg of the pTAR‑0‑hyg plasmid with KpnI (the cassette is flanked by two KpnI sites) following the restriction‑enzyme manufacturer’s buffer, temperature and incubation recommendations.

steps.title: Gel‑purify PCR products and digested backbone
steps.instruction: Run the PCR amplicons and the KpnI‑digested plasmid on an agarose gel, excise the correct bands, and extract DNA with a gel‑extraction kit, eluting in the smallest feasible volume (≤ 20 µl). Optional: clean the eluate with a Zyppy Clean & Concentrator kit and elute in 5 µl for higher purity.

steps.title: Assemble fragments using Gibson assembly
steps.instruction: In a tube, combine the purified 5'UTR, 3'UTR, and backbone fragments with NEBuilder Gibson assembly mix, using 1–5 µl of each fragment as recommended by the kit.

steps.title: Transform E. coli and recover colonies
steps.instruction: Introduce the Gibson assembly reaction into 50 µl thermocompetent E. coli and recover transformants.

substeps.instruction: Add 1–5 µl of the Gibson assembly mix to the 50 µl competent cells.
Incubate on ice for 10–30 min.
Heat‑shock at 42 °C for 30–40 s in a water bath.
Return to ice for 5–10 min.
Add 750 µl SOC medium.
Incubate at 37 °C, 250 rpm for 1 h.

steps.title: Concentrate cells and plate on selective media
steps.instruction: Optional concentration step followed by plating on kanamycin‑selective LB agar.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the recovered culture at 2000 × g for 2–5 min.
Discard most of the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 100–200 µl leftover supernatant.
Plate 5 µl, 20 µl and the remaining volume on LB agar containing 30 µg/ml kanamycin.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Screen colonies by PCR for correct assembly
steps.instruction: Perform colony PCR on individual colonies using primers JD281, JD333, JD306, JD288, and JD445. Expected band sizes for ~500 bp flanking regions: JD281+JD333 = 828 bp, JD281+JD306 = 1124 bp, JD288+JD445 = 848 bp. Run products on a gel to confirm the presence of the assembled flanking regions.

steps.title: Prepare glycerol stocks and isolate plasmid
steps.instruction: For colonies giving the expected PCR bands, grow a single colony in 5 ml LB + 30 µg/ml kanamycin overnight at 37 °C, 250 rpm. Then create a glycerol stock and isolate the plasmid.

substeps.instruction: Incubate overnight culture as described.
Mix 700 µl of the culture with 300 µl 50 % glycerol and store at –80 °C.
Perform a mini‑prep on the remaining 4 ml, elute DNA, and adjust concentration to ~100 ng/µl.
Sequence the plasmid across the flanking regions using the appropriate primers.

steps.title: Electroporate verified plasmid into Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: Electroporate the sequence‑verified plasmid into the chosen Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain. Recover cells and plate on LB agar containing rifampicin 50 µg/ml and kanamycin 30 µg/ml. Incubate at 25 °C until colonies appear.

steps.title: Verify Agrobacterium colonies by PCR
steps.instruction: Optionally perform colony PCR on Agrobacterium transformants using the same primer set as in the E. coli screening step to confirm presence of the knockout construct.

steps.title: Select and grow Agrobacterium transformants
steps.instruction: Inoculate a confirmed Agrobacterium colony into 50 ml LB containing rifampicin 50 µg/ml and kanamycin 30 µg/ml. Grow overnight at 27 °C, 250 rpm.

steps.title: Induce Agrobacterium with acetosyringone
steps.instruction: Prepare Agrobacterium for plant infection by inducing with acetosyringone.

substeps.instruction: Harvest the overnight culture and centrifuge at 3000 × g, 4 °C for 20–30 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 50 ml Induction Medium (IM).
Measure OD600 and adjust the suspension to ~0.5 (e.g., if OD600 = 0.3 add 30 ml IM; if 0.4 add 40 ml).
Add acetosyringone to a final concentration of 0.2 mM (add 50 µl of 0.2 M stock per 50 ml).
Incubate at 27 °C, 150 rpm for approximately 5 hours.

steps.title: Harvest and count fungal spores
steps.instruction: Collect spores from a sporulating fungal culture and determine concentration.

substeps.instruction: Flush a spore‑producing plate with sterile H2O.
Pass the wash through a syringe packed with sterile cotton wool.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 3000–5000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the spore pellet in sterile H2O.
Count spores using a haemocytometer and adjust concentration as needed.

steps.title: Co‑culture spores with Agrobacterium on membrane
steps.instruction: Mix spores with induced Agrobacterium and place on a nitrocellulose membrane over induction agar.

substeps.instruction: Mix 100 µl spore suspension (optimal concentration to be determined) with 100 µl induced Agrobacterium (OD600 ≈ 0.5).
Place a 0.45 µm, 47 mm nitrocellulose membrane onto an IM agar plate containing 0.2 mM acetosyringone.
Spread the 200 µl mixture evenly onto the membrane (use 3–10 plates per transformation).
Wrap the plate with parafilm or cling‑wrap and incubate at 25 °C in the dark for 2–5 days.

steps.title: Select fungal transformants on antibiotic plates
steps.instruction: Transfer membranes to selective fungal medium and allow colonies to develop.

substeps.instruction: Place each membrane onto ½ PDA plates supplemented with hygromycin 50 µg/ml, cefotaxime 50 µg/ml, and streptomycin 30 µg/ml.
Wrap plates and incubate at 25 °C in the dark until fungal colonies appear.

steps.title: Validate fungal knockouts by PCR
steps.instruction: Confirm correct integration of the hygromycin cassette and loss of the target gene in fungal colonies.

substeps.instruction: Transfer each emerging colony to a fresh selective plate (one colony per plate).
Perform a quick DNA extraction.
Run PCR with primers 5UTR‑seq + JD288 and 3UTR‑seq + JD333 to verify junctions, and with primers specific for the original gene of interest.
Correct knock‑outs show bands for both UTR‑junctions and no band for the native gene.

steps.title: Optional: sequence knockout region
steps.instruction: Amplify a region extending beyond the UTRs (using primers 5UTR‑seq + JD288 and 3UTR‑seq + JD333) and sequence to confirm precise integration of the hygromycin cassette.
